result.title: How Well Do LLMs Reason with Noisy Evidence? An Active Visual Reasoning Benchmark
result.summary: Real-world reasoning rarely reduces to static question answering: agents must actively gather information from tools and sensors that are often noisy and unreliable. Yet most existing active reasoning benchmarks assume that environmental feedback is trustworthy, or introduce noise without exposing an explicit, calibrated uncertainty signal, leaving open how LLMs should reason when the evidence itself is uncertain. We introduce VisualNoiseQA, a novel benchmark for active reasoning under noisy visual feedback. A text-only LLM must solve VQA problems by iteratively querying a fixed, off-the-shelf VLM treated as a stochastic visual sensor. For each query, we draw multiple samples and expose an empirical uncertainty signal via self-consistency, enabling the reasoner to probe from different angles and decide what to ask next and when to stop. Our construction is automatic and scalable: starting from diverse VQA sources and two noisy VLMs, we retain only questions where the sensor is inconsistent yet human-solvable. We evaluate multiple LLM reasoners on 1,000 instances spanning perception, chart understanding, and knowledge-intensive reasoning. VisualNoiseQA thus provides a controlled playground to study how different LLMs exploit uncertainty signals for robust reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 VisualNoiseQA 基准：文本 LLM 需通过迭代查询一个固定的、带随机性的 VLM（视作噪声视觉传感器）来解决 VQA，每次查询多次采样并给出自一致性不确定性信号，评估 1000 个感知、图表理解与知识推理实例中的主动推理表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益与成本问题：不确定性信号驱动的“问什么、何时停”决策，以及噪声视觉证据的筛选与利用，可供核查 latent 推理中证据获取与停止准则的设计。
